\label{lemma-huge-diagram}
Given a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
& 0 \ar[r] & N_2 \ar[r] & B'_2 \ar[r] & B_2 \ar[r] & 0 \\
& 0 \ar[r]|\hole & I_2 \ar[u]_{c_2} \ar[r] &
A'_2 \ar[u] \ar[r]|\hole & A_2 \ar[u] \ar[r] & 0 \\
0 \ar[r] & N_1 \ar[ruu] \ar[r] & B'_1 \ar[r] & B_1 \ar[ruu] \ar[r] & 0 \\
0 \ar[r] & I_1 \ar[ruu]|\hole \ar[u]^{c_1} \ar[r] &
A'_1 \ar[ruu]|\hole \ar[u] \ar[r] & A_1 \ar[ruu]|\hole \ar[u] \ar[r] & 0
}
$$
with front and back solutions to (\ref{equation-to-solve}) we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item There exist a canonical element in
$\Ext^1_{B_1}(\NL_{B_1/A_1}, N_2)$
whose vanishing is a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence
of a ring map $B'_1 \to B'_2$ fitting into the diagram.
\item If there exists a map $B'_1 \to B'_2$ fitting into the diagram
the set of all such maps is a principal homogeneous space under
$\Hom_{B_1}(\Omega_{B_1/A_1}, N_2)$.
\end{enumerate}

statement:
Let $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings with square-zero kernel $I$; let $A\to B$ be an $A$-algebra, $N$ a $B$-module, and $c:I\to N$ an $A$-linear map. A solution of the lifting problem is a commutative diagram of ring homomorphisms with exact rows $0\to I\to A'\to A\to0$ and $0\to N\to B'\to B\to0$ in which $N\subset B'$ is square-zero, $B'$ is an $A'$-algebra and the induced map $I\to N$ equals $c$. Isomorphisms of solutions commute with the maps from $A'$ and to $B$ and are the identity on the identified $N$.

For a homomorphism of rings $A\to B$ choose a polynomial presentation $P=A[E]\twoheadrightarrow B$ with kernel $J$. The naive cotangent complex $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}$ is the two-term complex $(J/J^2\xrightarrow{d}\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB)$ in cohomological degrees $-1,0$, well defined up to quasi-isomorphism. The module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{B/A}$ is its $H^0$. The notation $\operatorname{Ext}_B^q(K,N)$ means $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(K,N[q])$. For ringed spaces, topoi, and schemes, $\mathrm{NL}$ denotes the corresponding locally defined complex of sheaves of modules.

isomorphism classes of solutions is principal homogeneous under
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}, N)$.

statement:
A first-order thickening $i:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ of ringed spaces is a morphism inducing a homeomorphism of underlying spaces, a surjection $\mathcal O_{X'}\twoheadrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_X$, and a square-zero kernel $\mathcal I$. Identify the underlying topological spaces, so $\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}/\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal I$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-module. More generally a thickening only requires the kernel to be locally nilpotent.

A morphism of first-order thickenings $(f,f')$ is a commuting square of ringed spaces $(X,\mathcal O_X)\xrightarrow{i}(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ over $(S,\mathcal O_S)\xrightarrow{t}(S',\mathcal O_{S'})$, with vertical morphisms $f:X\to S$ and $f':X'\to S'$. Put $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_{X'}\to\mathcal O_X)$ and $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_{S'}\to\mathcal O_S)$. The induced homomorphism $(f')^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal I$ equals $f^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal I$ for first-order thickenings. The morphism of thickenings is called strict if this map is surjective.

For the commutative square of ringed-space thickenings above the morphism $(f, f')$
is a strict morphism of thickenings if and only if
that commuting square is cartesian in the category
of ringed spaces.

Identify the underlying topological spaces, so $\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}/\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal I$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-module. More generally a thickening only requires the kernel to be locally nilpotent.

For a first-order thickening of ringed spaces with ideal $\mathcal I$, an extension of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal K$ on the thickened space means a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal K\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to0$ of $\mathcal O_{X'}$-modules, with $\mathcal I$ annihilating the two end terms. It induces an $\mathcal O_X$-linear action map $c_{\mathcal F'}:\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\to\mathcal K$, defined by $c_{\mathcal F'}(a\otimes s)=a\tilde s$ for a local lift $\tilde s\in\mathcal F'$ of $s$. Isomorphisms of extensions fix their identified end terms.

Let $i : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (X', \mathcal{O}_{X'})$
be a first order thickening of ringed spaces.
Let $\mathcal{F}'$, $\mathcal{G}'$ be $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-modules and set
$\mathcal{F} = i^*\mathcal{F}'$ and $\mathcal{G} = i^*\mathcal{G}'$.
Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_X$-linear map.
There exists an element
$$
o(\varphi) \in
\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal{O}_X}(Li^*\mathcal{F}',
\mathcal{I}\mathcal{G}')
$$
whose vanishing is a necessary and sufficient condition for the
existence of a lift of $\varphi$ to an $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-linear map
$\varphi' : \mathcal{F}' \to \mathcal{G}'$.
